local_idea_assessment.allowed_scope: bounded assessment of an extension not covered by this tree, in an isolated local branch

ai_use.scope: proposed planning content, structured metadata, document and diagram renderer

nodes.title: Reopen scope
nodes.question: Has delivery closed, and has the owner explicitly reopened a bounded research scope?
nodes.relevance: Protect delivery and preserve a reproducible baseline before investing in extensions.
nodes.scope: Retain baseline, studies, failures and delivery evidence; select one next experiment. A new explicit owner decision may replace the freeze.
nodes.acceptance: Record the exact scope decision and applicable delivery/endorsement evidence. Local assessment of unlisted ideas is the limited exception below; it grants no integration or milestone acceptance.
nodes.stop: D-DEL-03 remains in force until explicitly changed. No branch merge, deployment or operational activation follows from this tree.

nodes.title: Auditable costs
nodes.question: Do planning, mission audit and accounting agree on the same complete itinerary?
nodes.relevance: A proposed route must fit the mission model and remaining resources.
nodes.scope: Shared scientific API under D-COST-02, typed activity/wait/model context and reviewed parameters; no expanded scenario.
nodes.acceptance: Independently compare directed motion, connector, service, wait and return within predeclared tolerances. Exercise interrupted work, budget boundaries and duplicate debit; identify exact model/profile/configuration and owner review.
nodes.stop: A projected profile, approval Boolean or one matching case cannot close agreement. Preserve scientific/model rejection gates where required.

nodes.title: Three executed roles
nodes.question: Do drone, rover and human contribute evidenced work under one mission authority?
nodes.relevance: Turn isolated components into an observable integrated mission.
nodes.scope: Same base case: survey, inspection, human work, contradiction, acknowledged stop, authorized replan and return.
nodes.acceptance: One run links orders, executed footprints, observations, map versions, poses, work intervals and resources. Require HALTED/zero speed/stable pose before replan. Retain no-alternative, unaffordable-return and optional-task accept/reject cases.
nodes.stop: Three markers, assignments or a scripted COMPLETE do not prove execution. Correct blocking is distinct from mission success.

nodes.title: Reproducible base
nodes.question: Can another member reproduce and audit the exact mission and its failures?
nodes.relevance: Attribute later improvements to a controlled change.
nodes.scope: Close scientific and gateway evidence, replay/video that same run and pin the comparison baseline.
nodes.acceptance: Retain source/config/input hashes, seeds, closed work/traversal/resource audit and exact run IDs. Replay offline on two machines with causal seek and same-run video. Repeat with N and tolerances agreed before evaluation; retain failures.
nodes.stop: Green CI or a video of another run does not close the gate. Do not change the control while evaluating an extension.

nodes.title: Multiscale context
nodes.question: Does 512-1024 m context improve selection of 128/256 m work windows?
nodes.relevance: Add geological context and meaningful station alternatives without confusing extent and detail.
nodes.scope: One supported candidate sector, same model and grid; regional context may remain outside the operational graph.
nodes.acceptance: Verify coverage, CRS/datum, NoData, native resolution, non-collinear controls and hashes. Declare load/search limits first; compare whether the larger context changes a justified science choice.
nodes.stop: Keep the smaller map if extra area is empty, misses the feature or exceeds limits. Never move A/B or inflate budgets to force success.

nodes.title: Opportunistic science
nodes.question: Can an observation during travel improve selection of secondary work?
nodes.relevance: Gain evidenced scientific value while preserving primary work and return.
nodes.scope: Explicit objectives and utility rubric, public discovery evidence and MissionManager assignment.
nodes.acceptance: Compare against a fixed plan under identical conditions. Record completed science under a reviewed rubric, rejected optional work, return and reserves. No hidden future-task catalogue reaches the runtime.
nodes.stop: Visited-POI count alone is not scientific value. Without defensible utility or a changed decision, do not add an optimizer.

nodes.title: Campaign atlas
nodes.question: Does the strategy remain useful across regions and campaign lengths?
nodes.relevance: Connect regional science selection, stations and campaign logistics.
nodes.scope: Multiple supported sectors with declared domain limits; no claim of operational Martian campaigns.
nodes.acceptance: External review of science/product coverage and campaign ledger; evaluate regions not used to tune the strategy and publish unsupported cases.
nodes.stop: Jezero success does not establish planetary generalization. Without comparable coverage/models, keep a catalogue of proposals.

nodes.title: Seeded worlds
nodes.question: Does the planner handle structurally different hypothetical worlds correctly?
nodes.relevance: Distinguish adaptation from a single scripted scene.
nodes.scope: H-DAN-01: bounded assumed relief, obstacles and footprints with fixed prior, model and budgets. Controlled families precede random seeds.
nodes.acceptance: Same seed/configuration yields the same array hash. Open/detour/blocked families show structural diversity. Keep evaluator worlds private and terrain/sensor/policy random streams separate; declare N and criteria before running.
nodes.stop: Do not select seeds for a preferred story. Different seeds may correctly yield the same route. Cosmetic noise is not structural diversity or new observed resolution.

nodes.title: Explore for value
nodes.question: Which observation reduces useful uncertainty before committing resources?
nodes.relevance: Justify reconnaissance by better decisions and its own costs.
nodes.scope: Compare no reconnaissance, corridor survey and informative survey on identical worlds.
nodes.acceptance: Measure success/return, total exploration cost, replans, rejected segments and science work, including failures. Require a predeclared benefit over simple policies with equal initial information/seeds.
nodes.stop: Global uncertainty reduction is insufficient without useful decisions. Keep the simple policy when benefit does not exceed cost.

nodes.title: Evaluated learning
nodes.question: Does a learned component improve results outside its training/tuning worlds?
nodes.relevance: Address a measured classical-method gap, if one exists.
nodes.scope: One perception or policy component per experiment; retain the classical baseline and separated labels/data.
nodes.acceptance: Split by worlds/sites, use unseen seeds, prevent leakage, retain uncertainty/rejection behavior and run an ablation. Demonstrate a predeclared improvement over the baseline.
nodes.stop: Discard if it fails to generalize or justify cost/robustness. Simulation success does not establish transfer to Mars or certification.

nodes.title: Dynamic assignment
nodes.question: Does changing who surveys or inspects improve an event-driven mission?
nodes.relevance: Make cooperation adaptive before adding robots.
nodes.scope: Same three agents, capabilities/orders/resources per ID and a single mission authority.
nodes.acceptance: Compare to fixed roles: one justified reassignment and one correctly rejected reassignment. Verify precedence, completed work, independent ledgers and nonconflicting orders/reserves.
nodes.stop: Keep fixed roles if no relevant case improves. A larger agent list is not cooperation.

nodes.title: Larger fleet
nodes.question: Does each additional agent deliver net useful work?
nodes.relevance: Increase coverage/redundancy only when they justify coordination and consumption.
nodes.scope: Increase N one step at a time; account for space, task and resource conflicts.
nodes.acceptance: Against three agents, measure marginal completed work, total cost/latency, conflicts and recovery from one failure. Predeclare compute limits and preserve identity on every order.
nodes.stop: Stop scaling when gain disappears or limits fail. More published states or drawn coverage do not count as executed work.

nodes.title: Resilient network
nodes.question: How does valid authority survive delayed, lost or unavailable communication?
nodes.relevance: Preserve coherence and return when information is not instantaneous.
nodes.scope: First degrade communications under central authority; decentralize only if necessary.
nodes.acceptance: Inject losses/reordering/partitions and test command expiry, stale maps, no double assignment and finite-resource wait/return behavior.
nodes.stop: Do not distribute decisions without verified authority/recovery rules. Silence cannot imply safe state or completed work.

nodes.title: Campaign / EVA / sorties
nodes.question: Which horizons/resources make cooperation useful on a real patch?
nodes.relevance: Avoid imposing the human demonstration horizon on the rover campaign.
nodes.scope: Separate rover campaign, human EVA and drone sorties with a global clock and cumulative ledger. Review CAM proposals without automatic adoption.
nodes.acceptance: Use actual mapped routes and reviewed work/wait/return costs, remaining availability between phases and joint sensitivity. Review allocations/parameters; nominal fit by construction is insufficient.
nodes.stop: Reject/reduce scope when adverse cases fail or a phase balance is missing. Longer time/battery allocations are not demonstrated hardware capacity.

nodes.title: Energy and environment
nodes.question: When does an environmental condition change a decision, with what uncertainty?
nodes.relevance: Make waiting, recharge or exposure influence planning through a justified model.
nodes.scope: One phenomenon at a time: generation/recharge, thermal state or environmental exposure under reviewed assumptions.
nodes.acceptance: Close cumulative balances with units/intervals and boundary cases. Identify sources/analogs, spatial/temporal transfer, sensitivity and missing-input rejection; compare with the model without this component.
nodes.stop: Do not derive safety thresholds from historical context or reset batteries. A display layer is not a validated predictive model.

nodes.title: Multi-sol campaigns
nodes.question: Does a longer campaign improve science/return without hidden inter-day consumption?
nodes.relevance: Plan prior scouting, rest, maintenance and work windows.
nodes.scope: Complete agenda, agent availability and contingencies; no assumption of real hardware autonomy.
nodes.acceptance: Close ledgers between sols, include sleep/heating/recharge/activity and interrupt/recover causally. Compare with a shorter campaign on equivalent objectives.
nodes.stop: No full-campaign authorization with NOT_ESTIMATED intervals or unmodeled resources. A sortie budget does not establish campaign capacity.

nodes.title: Hierarchical planning
nodes.priority: Only after a measured scale bottleneck
nodes.question: Does regional/local decomposition preserve solution quality and constraints?
nodes.relevance: Keep useful response times once larger area adds scientific value.
nodes.scope: One hierarchical strategy on the same problem/model; keep the baseline solver as reference.
nodes.acceptance: Compare reference-solvable cases, costs/return, p50/p95 latency, memory and UNKNOWN reasons. Include corridor/locality counterexamples; declare any loss of optimality.
nodes.stop: Do not add hierarchy if the solver already meets limits or the approximation loses important alternatives. Do not hide scaling by raising timeouts.

nodes.title: Incremental replanning
nodes.priority: Only after correctness and useful reuse
nodes.question: Can reuse accelerate changes without preserving obsolete information?
nodes.relevance: Reduce repeated work while retaining declared guarantees.
nodes.scope: One search/cache mechanism; preserve map, cost and authorization semantics.
nodes.acceptance: Compare full recomputation under map changes, removed obstacles, changed costs and continuous poses. Test invalidation and measure benefit at equal load.
nodes.stop: An incorrect cache hit fails acceptance. Keep simple recomputation without reproducible benefit or with stale answers.

nodes.title: Multiobjective decisions
nodes.question: Does the team need alternatives that one objective cannot express?
nodes.relevance: Expose science/time/consumption/uncertainty tradeoffs.
nodes.scope: A bounded set of explainable alternatives, measurable objectives and mission/human selection.
nodes.acceptance: Show useful changed decisions, verify dominance and each alternative's budget/return, test sensitivity and keep compute cost bounded.
nodes.stop: SAFE is not certification and science utility cannot be arbitrary. Without justified preferences, present alternatives without automatic authorization.

nodes.title: Audited simulated sensor
nodes.question: Does partial/noisy observation yield a causal and useful update?
nodes.relevance: Make acquired information depend on executed exploration and sensor limits.
nodes.scope: One modality with declared footprint/occlusion/noise; reference or full world isolated from planner.
nodes.acceptance: Derive footprints from executed poses, quantify uncertainty/latency, reject stale/duplicate data and apply updates atomically. Compare error to reference only in evaluation.
nodes.stop: Orbital preview is not observation. Do not expose a full world or infer metric properties from appearance without calibration.

nodes.title: Physics and localization
nodes.question: Do slip, relief or pose error change model limits and decisions?
nodes.relevance: Measure errors absent from kinematic execution.
nodes.scope: Gazebo or another reviewed environment for one bounded capability with identified parameters and reference trials.
nodes.acceptance: Contrast trajectories/consumption against an independent trial reference, set error limits beforehand and test stopping on contradictory pose/observation.
nodes.stop: A more detailed simulator does not validate its parameters. Without model identification, report synthetic sensitivity only.

nodes.title: Analog field trial
nodes.question: Does perception-planning-execution retain behavior in a limited physical trial?
nodes.relevance: Contrast assumptions outside simulation and identify transfer failures.
nodes.scope: Hardware-in-the-loop, then a controlled terrestrial analog with expert supervision and bounded operation.
nodes.acceptance: Review protocol/limits, independent telemetry/reference, stop criteria, failures/recovery and external repetition. Separate calibration and evaluation.
nodes.stop: Do not extrapolate a terrestrial analog to a Mars EVA. Operational autonomy/certification needs additional institutions and validation.
